title: Welcome & detective setup
notes: A story, then an action
A two-column desktop composition balances the learning promise with a short setup form. The illustration stays a labeled placeholder.
One clear first step
Name, partner, colour, then the primary action. No account creation interrupts the child’s first investigation.
Quiet, persistent controls
Language, sound preference and desk mode sit in the header. Grayscale separates hierarchy from final brand colours.

title: Casebook & learning units
notes: Progress has a place
A greeting leads the page. Cases solved, rank and XP sit beside it without competing with the next activity.
Four independent tracks
All four units are available. Each unit shows its own progress; individual cases unlock in sequence within that unit.
A clear next action
The current case receives the largest card. Two upcoming cases appear below; replayable solved cases sit in a disclosure.

title: The clue workspace
notes: Read before doing
Unit, case number, skill, title and a single mission establish the task before interactive clues appear.
Objects before destinations
The clue tray precedes three evidence bags. Tap a clue and a bag, or drag it directly. Undo and Reset make exploration reversible.
Check when ready
The primary Check action sits at the end of the workspace. Hints and the no-timer reminder have a separate, calm footer.

title: First-use movement guide
notes: Explain the gesture
The modal demonstrates drag and tap as equal ways to move a clue. The production site animates this guidance.
Keep the activity in view
A muted backdrop preserves context. The explanation sits above the existing board rather than on a new page.
Easy to dismiss
A close button, Escape, and “Let me try” return focus to the task. Reopen the guide from “How to move”.

title: Hints without pressure
notes: One idea at a time
A short prompt supports thinking without revealing the completed arrangement. The step count sets expectations.
Visual support
An unfinished visual example reinforces the method. Back and Another hint let the learner set the pace.
Return to the same task
“Let me try” closes the dialog. Clue placements remain intact, and hints carry no penalty.

title: Supportive retry feedback
notes: Feedback stays local
Only groups needing review receive a dashed border and “Look again” label. The correct group keeps its neutral appearance.
Keep the learner in control
The board is preserved. A clue move, Undo or Reset clears the review state so the learner can try again.
No countdown, no penalty
A brief explanation encourages equal sharing. The primary action remains Check; hints are still available.

title: Success & next-case progression
notes: Celebrate in context
The result appears below the completed groups. The learner can connect the arrangement with the outcome.
Make progress tangible
The first solve awards 100 XP, raises the detective to level 2 and unlocks the next case. Replays do not add XP.
A natural continuation
“Next case” leads to the next activity. The header and casebook also reflect the updated progress.

title: Explore data & choose an answer
notes: Tools before the chart
Bars show, Filter, Sort and View each pair a label with a short explanation. The mobile layout uses two columns.
Read the evidence
Horizontal bars leave room for category labels. Values stay off bars to practise scale reading; table view offers exact numbers.
An intentional answer
Select Event, filter Blue, then choose the event with the most points. Both the tool setup and the answer are checked.

title: Edit the detective profile
notes: A familiar form
Reuse the setup fields and ordering, with the detective’s current name and partner already selected.
Focus on the edit
A compact single-column form limits distractions. Save profile returns to the casebook.
Production placement
The existing website opens this form in a dialog. This standalone specimen exposes the fields for proposal review.
